title: The Distant Colony
premise: Ansel Lockridge, sole caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, runs supply routes between colonies that severed contact generations ago. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, she traces it to Meridian Station, where half of humanity's last colonists sleep in cryosleep while the other half's descendants have built a fragile society above. The station's ruling council plans to wake only their own lineage before Earth's final transmission loop decays forever, erasing the coordinates of the sleeping thousands. Ansel must choose between the found family she builds among the station's outcasts and the legal order that keeps the colony alive — and in the end, she broadcasts the loop one last time herself, waking all of the sleepers and accepting exile as the price of justice.
about_author: August Montrose is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent a decade listening to dead frequencies before turning to fiction. They write from a converted signal station on the northern coast, where the static still comes in on clear nights.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She tends the seed vault alone, cataloguing what Earth left behind, then departs on her annual run between silent colonies. Establishes her isolation and quiet competence. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like a uniform, and the small comfort of routine.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Air
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Mid-route, her receiver catches a distress call in Old Standard, a language unused for two centuries. She triangulates it to Meridian Station, officially decommissioned. Against protocol, she alters course. Emotional beat: the first crack in her solitude — someone out there is speaking her ancestors' tongue.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She docks at Meridian and finds a living colony hiding beneath derelict hulls, ruled by the Council of Continuity. A young mechanic, Ivo Sarn, smuggles her inside. She learns the cryo-bays hold ten thousand sleepers — including the senders of the signal. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Council of Continuity
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with interludes from Councilor Vess Hale. Vess offers Ansel supplies and safe harbor if she carries no messages out. Ansel glimpses the waking schedule: only Council bloodlines will be revived before Earth's transmission loop fails. Emotional beat: the seduction of safety offered at a moral price.

chapters.title: The Sleeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo reveals his mother sleeps in Bay Nine; he was born awake, a 'temp' with no rights. He shows Ansel the sabotage network among temps planning to force a full awakening. Ansel refuses to commit — until Vess orders the bays' power rationed, dooming the oldest sleepers. Emotional beat: found family forming in defiance.

chapters.title: Rationing
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess justifies the triage: the loop decays in months, and waking everyone means no one survives the transition. Her chapters humanize the antagonist — she lost children to an earlier failed thaw. Meanwhile Ansel copies the bay manifests. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into policy.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The temps seize the transmitter to broadcast the loop themselves, but the Council scrambles its defenses. In the chaos, Ivo is captured and Ansel escapes to her ship with the full manifest and the loop's final coordinates. Emotional beat: betrayal of trust, and the cost of choosing a side.

chapters.title: What the Loop Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, alone in orbit. She discovers the loop contains more than coordinates — it holds Earth's last confession: the sleepers were exiled deliberately, deemed genetically expendable. Justice outside the law becomes literal: there is no law here, only who tells the story. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Names
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Ansel and Vess. Ansel returns, offering Vess a bargain: joint broadcast, shared blame, full awakening. Vess refuses; the temps rise; the transmitter burns. Ansel reroutes her ship's own array into the station grid and reads all ten thousand names aloud as the bays open. Emotional beat: sacrifice — her ship, her route, her old life, burned for the many.

chapters.title: First Light
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, months later. The awakened emerge into a station remade under a provisional charter written by temps and Councilors alike; Vess, exiled to the surface farms, tends the first crops from Ansel's vault seeds. Ansel stays — not as caretaker of the past, but citizen of something new. Emotional beat: home found not inherited but chosen.
